messages.subject: categorical / softmax functions not found?
parts:

This is the R sessionInfo result:

This is the error:

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  :
  failed to parse Stan model 'X.model' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=89, column=13

                        Y[i,j] ~ categorical(prob[i,j]);
            ^-- here

    arg 0 type=int

prob[i,j] is a vector. I've received a similar error with the softmax function, although could parameterize the model without using that.

I apologize if this has been addressed elsewhere. I've done some searches but didn't find much.

Thanks!

0.  categorical_log(int, vector) : real
unknown distribution=categorical

prob[i,j] is a vector. I've received a similar error with the softmax function, although could parameterize the model without using that.

Can you tell us the declaration of prob (or just attach the whole .stan file)? It looks like prob is a three-dimensional array, in which case prob[i,j] would seek like a vector conceptually but is not actually a vector in the Stan sense. I think prob needs to be declared as an array of vectors, something like

vector prob[N,K];

Ben

messages.author: 1781f73f3258f999
messages.subject: Re: categorical / softmax functions not found?
parts:
On Thursday, July 25, 2013 1:22:39 PM UTC-5, Ben Goodrich wrote:

Can you tell us the declaration of prob (or just attach the whole .stan file)? It looks like prob is a three-dimensional array, in which case prob[i,j] would seek like a vector conceptually but is not actually a vector in the Stan sense. I think prob needs to be declared as an array of vectors, something like

vector prob[N,K];

Ben

Thanks!

That seems to have done the trick.

I was declaring prob as a three-dimensional array, e.g.,

real prob[N,J,K];

Declaring it as a two-dimensional array of vectors--e.g.,

vector[K] prob[N,J];

got rid of the error message.
